description: This chart illustrates the distribution of character roles – Hero, Victim, and Villain – across four different political biases: Left bias, Left-center bias, No source, and Right bias. The horizontal axis displays the political bias categories, labeled “Left bias”, “Left center bias”, “No source”, and “Right bias”, in that order from left to right. The vertical axis, labeled “Proportion”, represents a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at 0.2 intervals. Each bias category is represented by a stacked bar. Each bar is composed of three colored segments: a blue segment representing “Hero”, a brown segment representing “Victim”, and a light blue segment representing “Villain”. For “Left bias”, the “Hero” segment reaches approximately 0.35, the “Victim” segment reaches approximately 0.1, and the “Villain” segment reaches approximately 0.55. For “Left center bias”, the “Hero” segment reaches approximately 0.25, the “Victim” segment reaches approximately 0.3, and the “Villain” segment reaches approximately 0.45. For “No source”, the “Hero” segment reaches approximately 0.3, the “Victim” segment reaches approximately 0.05, and the “Villain” segment reaches approximately 0.65. For “Right bias”, the “Hero” segment reaches approximately 0.2, the “Victim” segment reaches approximately 0.15, and the “Villain” segment reaches approximately 0.65. The bars are not sorted, and no bars are visually emphasized.
